components.note: Study/report, outcome and result units defined; four availability states (unidentified study, identified study without usable result, partial result, selected result) separated; within-study missing participants and not-measured vs withheld distinguished; unknown measurement status said not to establish either case; motive not inferred from absence. Failure condition does not hold.

Finite selection model, conditional available law q=ps/rho, mean shift Cov/rho, reconstruction under specified s>0, explicit nonidentification counterexample and zero-selection support failure, all proved in full in the annex; stages of selection listed and direction/motive caveats given.

Bibliographic, register, results-register, regulatory/CSR, sponsor and protocol/SAP strategies with stated limitations (plans not results, redaction, interested-party data, unannounced amendments); inception cohorts with limits (outcomes still missing, frame completeness, registration adoption, changed eligibility) and a proved target-accounting theorem; documented Eyding example with denominator caveat.

ROB-ME scope, results matrix, planning questions 3.1-3.3, signalling questions 4.1-4.8 with response options and applicability, suggested judgement paths with not-a-sum caveat and NA handling; sensitivity reasoning with proved missing-weight bounds, tipping point, random-effects reweighting limit, selection-model and regression-extrapolation cautions. Source held (held-sources.json entries for source/references/missing-evidence-cochrane-2024/chapter13-current-retrieved-2026-10-01.html and source/references/missing-evidence-cochrane-2024/rob-me-cribsheet-20231001.pdf); locators opened: ch13 sec. 13.2.2 (inception cohort, registration limits) and sec. 13.3.4.4 (>=10 studies, low power) / Table 13.3.b (sources of asymmetry) show the cited content; crib sheet pp. 6-8 (4.1-4.7 response options) and p. 14-15 Table 1 (judgement algorithm) show the cited content.

Funnel plot construction and reference flanks with caveats; list of small-study-effect causes; complete-cohort asymmetric case; theorem with written proof that one asymmetric plot has positive probability under chance, heterogeneity and selection models; contour and test limits (>=10 studies, low power, scale-specific tests). Asymmetry is explicitly not assigned a unique cause.
